title: Call Complexity of Arbitrary-Arity Correlation Intractability
summary: The result covers evasive relations only at constant arity; whether arbitrary-arity correlation intractability requires six random-function calls or fewer remains open.

formal_statement.body: For correlation intractability against evasive relations of arity $k$, a known result fully covers such relations only when $k=O(1)$, and its proof inherently fails for larger arities. Determine whether six calls to a random function are necessary to achieve correlation intractability for arbitrary arity, or whether fewer calls suffice.

scope.domain: Correlation intractability against evasive relations in block-cipher and Feistel-construction design.
parameters: Arity k of the evasive relation
Number of random-function calls as the resource complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether arbitrary-arity correlation intractability requires six random-function calls or can be achieved with fewer.

citations.label: Naor-Reingold Goes Public: The Complexity of Known-Key Security

progress.summary: The paper's two-call construction covers every fixed constant arity, but its proof does not fully cover larger arities. It leaves determining whether six calls are necessary for arbitrary arity or fewer suffice as future work.
citation_labels: Pratik Soni et al., Naor-Reingold Goes Public: The Complexity of Known-Key Security
